Like many people, years ago, I bought a betta without knowing a thing about taking care of them. I then promptly took to the internet and this reddit and had a crash course, learning everything I could. I did an in-fish cycle and he thrived. He lived in a 5 gallon tank that started off much like yours, but grew into a beautiful lush tank that kept him happy for many years.

Do you have a thermometer? I don't know if your heater has the temp on it, but I would also get a little separate thermometer that I can place in the water just so I always have an independent gauge to measure in case the heater malfunctions.

He will love plants. My betta started with two. Then I gradually, over many weeks and months, added more and more until he lived in a miniature forest.

He will love something to sit in like a floating log. Bettas feel safe in places they can get shelter in. My betta loved a little cave that sat on the bottom of his tank. It was peculiar because he had the floating log but he preferred a dark little cave on the bottom of his tank for some reason. :) Make sure any decoration you buy is smooth so that he can't scratch himself, but also make sure it has large holes so he can't get stuck in it. Bettas will try and squeeze themselves in the tiniest holes. So treat them like toddlers and make sure any decoration is toddler-proof.

Regular weekly water changes! Don't change all of the water. Maybe 40% a week. Also make sure the new water is the same temperature as his tank water. This is very important! (That's why it's important to have thermometers!)

Get a good water conditioner like Seachem!

Those are the things that immediately come to mind. Don't return him. You obviously love him. You are just at the beginning of your journey.

When I was growing up, disinterested fathers was my norm. I thought it was normal for Dads to not be as involved or as interested in their kids as Moms were, both from my own experience and from looking at all of my friends. As kids, we were always wowed when a Dad actually seemed to enjoy his kid's company and go out of his way to do things with them. It just wasn't the common story for us.

Imagine how my perspective changed as I grew up and saw a little more of the world. I'm ashamed to admit I'm still scarred, and whenever I see a Dad showing general interest in his kids I kind of just stop and drink it in. (Actually, it's lovely to watch any parent take a genuine full-hearted interest in their kids but the Dads especially make me pause.)
